s9-implement-stack-using-arrays.trick: Keep the top index one past the last value. Push writes at that index; pop decreases it. A fixed-capacity array makes overflow explicit.

s9-implement-queue-using-arrays.trick: Use a circular array: front points to the first element and size tracks occupancy. Wrap the insert position modulo capacity.

s9-implement-stack-using-queue.trick: After pushing a new value into one queue, rotate every older value behind it. The new value then sits at the front as the stack top.

s9-implement-queue-using-stack.trick: Push into an input stack. For front/pop, move input to output only when output is empty; each item moves at most once.
s9-implement-queue-using-stack.time: O(1) amortized per operation; O(n) worst-case front/pop

s9-implement-stack-using-linkedlist.trick: Treat the linked-list head as the stack top. Push and pop change only the head link.

s9-implement-queue-using-linkedlist.trick: Keep both head and tail pointers. Enqueue at the tail and dequeue at the head; reset tail when the queue becomes empty.

s9-check-for-balanced-paranthesis.trick: Push opening brackets. Each closing bracket must match the latest unmatched opening bracket; the stack must be empty at the end.

s9-implement-min-stack.trick: Store the minimum so far alongside every pushed value. Then top, pop, and getMin all take constant time.

s9-infix-to-postfix-conversion-using-sta.trick: Send operands directly to output. Hold operators on a stack, popping higher precedence first; '^' is right-associative.

s9-prefix-to-infix-conversion.trick: Scan prefix right to left. Push operands; for an operator, pop left then right and wrap their infix form in parentheses.

s9-prefix-to-postfix-conversion.trick: Scan prefix right to left. For each operator, pop its left and right expressions, then append the operator after both.

s9-postfix-to-prefix-conversion.trick: Scan postfix left to right. For an operator, pop right then left, and place the operator before them.

s9-postfix-to-infix.trick: Scan postfix left to right. For an operator, pop right then left and combine them as a parenthesized infix expression.

s9-convert-infix-to-prefix-notation.trick: Use operator and expression stacks. Apply higher-precedence operators first, building operator+left+right; keep '^' right-associative.

s9-next-greater-element.trick: Scan from right to left with a decreasing stack. Remove values no greater than the current one; the remaining top is its next greater value.

s9-next-greater-element-2.trick: For a circular array, scan indices 2n-1 down to 0 and index modulo n. The second pass supplies candidates beyond the physical end.

s9-next-smaller-element.trick: Scan from right to left with an increasing stack. Remove values at least as large as the current one.

s9-number-of-nges-to-the-right.trick: Scan the array from right to left. A Fenwick tree counts values already seen; subtract the count of values <= a[i] to get greater values to the right.
s9-number-of-nges-to-the-right.time: O(n log n + q), q queries

s9-trapping-rainwater.trick: The lower of the two boundary heights limits water on its side. Move that pointer inward, tracking its best boundary.

s9-sum-of-subarray-minimum.trick: For each element, count subarrays where it is the chosen minimum. A monotonic stack finds the previous strictly smaller and next smaller-or-equal boundaries.

s9-asteroid-collision.trick: A collision is possible only when a right-moving survivor meets a new left-moving asteroid. Resolve larger magnitudes until one side survives.

s9-sum-of-subarray-ranges.trick: Compute each element's contribution as a subarray maximum and as a minimum, using monotonic stacks; subtract the two sums.

s9-remove-k-digits.trick: Maintain a nondecreasing digit stack. When a smaller digit arrives, remove larger preceding digits while removals remain; strip leading zeroes at the end.

s9-largest-rectangle-in-a-histogram.trick: Keep increasing bar indices. When a shorter bar appears, pop taller bars and use the new top as each popped bar's left boundary.

s9-maximal-rectangles.trick: Treat each row as the base of a histogram of consecutive 1s above it. The largest histogram rectangle over all rows is the answer.

s9-sliding-window-maximum.trick: Keep indices in a deque with decreasing values. Drop indices outside the window; the front is its maximum.

s9-stock-span-problem.trick: Collapse earlier prices no greater than today's price. Each stack item stores its price and the span it already represents.

s9-the-celebrity-problem.trick: Eliminate one of each pair: if A knows B, A cannot be the celebrity; otherwise B cannot. Verify the one remaining candidate.

s9-lru-cache-important.trick: Use a doubly linked list for recency order and a hash map from key to list iterator. Move accessed keys to the front; evict from the back.

s9-lfu-cache.trick: Map keys to value/frequency and their position in a frequency list. Evict the least recently used key from the lowest-frequency list.
